{{Short description|German chemist (born 1972)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2026}}

'''Frank Klaus Glorius''' (born 1972 in [[Walsrode]]) is a German chemist and W3-Professor of organic chemistry in the Department of Chemistry and Pharmacy at the [[University of Münster]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/Chemie.oc/glorius/|title=Group Glorius|website=www.uni-muenster.de}}</ref>

== Life and work ==
Glorius studied chemistry at the [[Leibniz University Hannover]], completing his Diploma thesis in 1997. During his Diploma he also undertook a nine-month research stay at [[Stanford University]] with [[Paul Wender (chemist)|Paul A. Wender]] in 1995/1996.<ref>Paul A. Wender, Frank Glorius u.&nbsp;a.: ''Transition Metal-Catalyzed [5 + 2] Cycloadditions of Allenes and Vinylcyclopropanes: First Studies of Endo-Exo Selectivity, Chemoselectivity, Relative Stereochemistry, and Chirality Transfer.'' In: ''Journal of the American Chemical Society.'' 121, 1999, pp.&nbsp;5348–5349, {{doi|10.1021/ja9903072}}.</ref>
Glorius completed his Doctorate in 2000 investigating "New chiral bis-oxazoline ligands for enantioselective catalysis" at the [[University of Basel]] with [[Andreas Pfaltz]]. His PhD was divided between the [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research|Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung]] (1997–1999) and the [[University of Basel]] (1999–2000). Between 2000 and 2001 Glorius completed a [[Postdoctoral research|Postdoc]] at [[Harvard University]] in [[Cambridge (Massachusetts)|Cambridge]], with [[David A. Evans]] exploring the [[Total synthesis]] of [[Aflastatin A]]. Following this, he worked with his mentor [[Alois Fürstner]] as an independent researcher/research group leader/Assistant Professor at the [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research|Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung]]. In 2004, before formal completion of the habilitation, he was awarded a position as C3-Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Marburg]]. Since August 2007, Glorius has been a Professor of Organic Chemistry at the [[University of Münster]], where he serves Dean of the Faculty of Chemistry and Pharmacy since 2022.

Professor Glorius' research program is dedicated to the development of new [[Catalysis|catalytic methodologies]] in organic chemistry. His research group explores a wide range of topics including the development and application of [[Persistent carbene|N-heterocyclic carbenes]] (NHCs) in catalysis,<ref>Matthew N. Hopkinson, Christian Richter, Michael Schedler, Frank Glorius: ''An overview of N-heterocyclic carbenes.'' In: ''Nature.'' 510, 2014, pp.&nbsp;485–496, {{doi|10.1038/nature13384}}.</ref> exploration and use of NHCs as surface modifyers, [[carbon–hydrogen bond activation|C–H activation]],<ref>Joanna Wencel-Delord, Frank Glorius: ''C–H bond activation enables the rapid construction and late-stage diversification of functional molecules.'' In: ''Nature Chemistry.'' 5, 2013, pp.&nbsp;369–375, {{doi|10.1038/nchem.1607}}.</ref> asymmetric [[organocatalysis]],<ref>Xavier Bugaut, Frank Glorius: ''Organocatalytic umpolung: ''N''-heterocyclic carbenes and beyond.'' In: ''Chemical Society Reviews.'' 41, 2012, pp.&nbsp;3511, {{doi|10.1039/C2CS15333E}}.</ref> chemo- and enantioselective hydrogenation of aromatic compounds,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Hydrogenation of fluoroarenes: Direct access to all- cis -(multi)fluorinated cycloalkanes|first1=Mario P.|last1=Wiesenfeldt|first2=Zackaria|last2=Nairoukh|first3=Wei|last3=Li|first4=Frank|last4=Glorius|date=12 September 2017|journal=Science|volume=357|issue=6354|pages=908–912|doi=10.1126/science.aao0270|pmid=28798044 |s2cid=206661894 |doi-access=free|bibcode=2017Sci...357..908W }}</ref> [[photoredox catalysis]] and energy transfer photocatalysis,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kleinmans |first1=Roman |last2=Pinkert |first2=Tobias |last3=Dutta |first3=Subhabrata |last4=Paulisch |first4=Tiffany O. |last5=Keum |first5=Hyeyun |last6=Daniliuc |first6=Constantin G. |last7=Glorius |first7=Frank |date=May 2022 |title=Intermolecular [2π+2σ]-photocycloaddition enabled by triplet energy transfer |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04636-x |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=605 |issue=7910 |pages=477–482 |doi=10.1038/s41586-022-04636-x |pmid=35314833 |bibcode=2022Natur.605..477K |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[heterogeneous catalysis]], [[Metal–organic framework|Metal–Organic Frameworks]]/MOFs, development and use of lipid analogs, and the development of reaction screening technologies.<ref>Karl D. Collins, Frank Glorius: ''A robustness screen for the rapid assessment of chemical reactions.'' In: ''Nature Chemistry.'' 5, 2013, pp.&nbsp;597–601, {{doi|10.1038/nchem.1669}}.</ref>

Former members of the group have gone on to have careers in both academia (e.g. Canada, China, France, Germany, India and Japan) and industry (BASF, Bayer, Evonik, Clariant, Axalta, Lanxess, Continental, Archimica, Mitsubishi, Novartis or Janssen Pharmaceutica (Johnson & Johnson) for instance).

== Honors and awards ==
'''Research Awards:''' Glorius has received numerous grants, prizes and awards. In his early career, he was awarded the Liebig-scholarship of the [[Fonds der Chemischen Industrie]] (2001–2004), the ORCHEM-Award for Scientists (2004), and the [[BASF]] Catalysis Award (2005). Of particular note was the [[Alfried-Krupp-Förderpreis für junge Hochschullehrer|Alfried Krupp Prize]] in 2006, for €1&nbsp;million, the [[Europäischer Forschungsrat|ERC]] Independent Researcher Starting Grant, worth €1.5&nbsp;million, in 2010, and the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]], in 2013, from the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|German Research Foundation]], valued at €2.5&nbsp;million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dfg.de/gefoerderte_projekte/wissenschaftliche_preise/leibniz-preis/2013/index.jsp|title=Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz-Preis 2013|website=www.dfg.de}}</ref>
Additionally, he has received the OMCOS Award in 2011, and the [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] Heterocyclic Chemistry Award in 2012. In 2013, he was elected as an honorary member of the Israel Chemical Society, and was named as "Highly Cited Researcher" in all the years since 2014 (currently till 2022).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://publons.com/awards/highly-cited/2021/|title=Highly Cited Researchers|website=publons.com}}</ref> Glorius also received the Novartis Chemistry Lectureship Award for 2014/2015 and the inaugurational SYNLETT Best Paper Award 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thieme.de/de/thieme-chemistry/journals-synthesis-synlett-best-paper-award-winners-2015-94854.htm|title=Journals: 2015 Winners - Thieme Chemistry - Georg Thieme Verlag|website=Thieme}}</ref> In 2017 he has received the Mukaiyama Award from The Society of Synthetic Organic Chemistry, Japan (SSOCJ).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ssocj.jp/award/mukaiyama/2017/announcement2017-2.pdf |title=Mukaiyama Award Announcement |access-date=15 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171216091121/https://www.ssocj.jp/award/mukaiyama/2017/announcement2017-2.pdf |archive-date=16 December 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Most recently, he was selected for the Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award of the American Chemical Society (ACS),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding/awards/national.html|title=National Awards|website=American Chemical Society}}</ref> for the Merck, Sharp & Dohme Award of the Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/find-a-prize/organic-division-mid-career-award-merck-sharp-and-dohme-award/|title=Organic Division mid-career award: Merck, Sharp & Dohme Award|website=Royal Society of Chemistry |date=10 September 2020 }}</ref> and for the French Gay-Lussac Humboldt Prize. Glorius also has received the [[Otto Bayer Award]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Announcement of Winners: 2022 Otto Bayer Award, Early Excellence in Science Awards & Ernst-Ludwig Winnacker Award |url=https://www.bayer-foundation.com/news-stories/science/announcement-winners-2022-otto-bayer-award-early-excellence-science-awards-ernst-ludwig-winnacker |access-date=2023-05-01 |website=Bayer Foundation |language=en}}</ref> Finally, in addition to the ERC Starting Grant in 2010, he successfully applied for ERC Advanced Grants in 2017 ("HyDream") and 2022 ("HighEnT").<ref>{{Cite web |title=EU Research Council awards Frank Glorius with "ERC Advanced Grant |url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/news/view.php?cmdid=13240&lang=en |access-date=2023-05-01 |website=www.uni-muenster.de | date=31 March 2023 }}</ref>

'''Teaching Award:''' In addition, in 2014 Frank Glorius was awarded by the students of the Department of Chemistry&Pharmacy of the WWU Muenster with the "Goldener Brendel" for excellence in teaching. For his achievements as PhD supervisor he has received the IPMI Faculty Advisor Award 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ipmi.org/?page=AwardPrograms|title=IPMI Homepage}}</ref>

Glorius sits on the boards of numerous committees and societies, including the Kuratorium (Board of Trustees) of the Fonds der Chemischen Industrie, the selection committee of the Humboldt foundation for incoming postdocs, the German Catalysis Society (GeCatS) and the Münster branch of the [[Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker|German Chemical Society]] (2011–2014).

In 2021 Frank Glorius was elected as a member of the National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of Members |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/frank-glorius/ |access-date=2023-05-01 |website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina |language=en-US}}</ref> and in 2022 he became a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Frank Glorius is a new member of the "Academia Europaea" |url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/news/view.php?cmdid=12730&lang=en |access-date=2023-05-01 |website=www.uni-muenster.de | date=20 July 2022 }}</ref>
